title: 179 pre-Hispanic objects discovered in remote Zoque cave in Chiapas
summary: Archaeologists from Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) have documented 179 pre-Hispanic objects inside a difficult-to-reach cave in the La Venta River canyon, in what the institute describes as one of the most significant archaeological discoveries made in the region in recent decades. The site, known as Mundo Zoque Cave, lies near the Arco del Tiempo, a monumental natural rock formation in the municipality of Cintalapa, Chiapas. Extending for more than 100 meters, the cave contained 13 ritual deposits filled with ceramic urns, bowls and incense burners, many decorated with human figures and representations of jaguars, owls and snakes. Preliminary analysis dates the material to the regional Late Classic period, around AD 600–900. The cave was first located by local guide Jairo Díaz Barreiro, who reported it to the INAH Chiapas Center in January 2026. title: Uman's world of color, memory and transformation comes alive in a major new monograph
summary: Few artists make color feel quite as physical as Uman. Across paintings that teem with circles, grids, eyes, plants, bodies, animals and mysterious signs, color is not merely decorative or expressive; it becomes a repository for experience. “Color is memory,” the artist has said, a phrase that supplies both the title and central idea of Lauren Cornell’s opening essay in Uman, an ambitious new monograph published by Monacelli in association with the Hessel Museum of Art at Bard College. The book accompanies Uman: In Between, the artist’s first institutional survey, organized by Cornell at the Hessel Museum of Art and on view from June 27 through November 29, 2026. Yet the publication is more than an exhibition catalogue. According to CCS Bard executive director Tom Eccles, it is the first volume to fully illustrate and analyze Uman’s practice, reproducing nearly twice as many works as appear in the exhibition. title: Colonel Harland Sanders memorabilia auction raises nearly $300,000
summary: The historic auction of Colonel Harland Sanders' personal collection generated just shy of $300,000 in sales, with more than 100 artifacts sold across 74 lots to collectors, historians, entrepreneurs, and fans around the world. Held July 28 at the Claudia Sanders Dinner House in Shelbyville, Kentucky, the auction attracted more than 500 bidders, both in person and online. The collection, preserved by the Settle family since their 1974 purchase of Blackwood Hall and the Claudia Sanders Dinner House directly from Colonel and Claudia Sanders, offered rare personal artifacts spanning Sanders' life, business career, and legacy. The top-selling item was Colonel Harland Sanders' Personal Handwritten Datebook and Working Planner, which sold for $30,000. Far more than a simple appointment book, the planner served as Sanders' personal working notebook in 1964, documenting observations, expenses, travel details, meals, business notes, and other aspects of his daily activities. title: New contemporary art exhibition explores island histories and the American experience
summary: Contemporary art brings together histories separated by oceans and generations in “Imagining an Archipelago: Art from Cuba, Guam, the Philippines, Puerto Rico, and Their Diasporas.” The exhibition, on view now through June 6, 2027 at the Colby College Museum of Art, includes approximately 50 sculptures, paintings, photographs and immersive video and multimedia installations, including six newly commissioned works. Each of the more than 40 artists featured have connections to the island communities of Cuba, Guam, the Philippines and Puerto Rico and use their artistic practice to consider the complexity of the American experience. “Imagining an Archipelago” is the first major exhibition to use contemporary art to examine the impact of extending Manifest Destiny beyond North America. title: Eminem to auction over 100 signed sneakers for Detroit youth charity
summary: Julien’s Auctions presents the Marshall Mathers Foundation Auction - a landmark benefit sale featuring more than 100 sneakers from the personal collection of Eminem. The lineup includes rare Jordan x Eminem collaborations and other iconic brands, with each pair personally signed by Eminem. This is the largest single-sale collection of Eminem material ever offered at public auction. All proceeds benefit the Marshall Mathers Foundation. View the auction and register to bid now at Julien's Auctions ahead of the August 25th sale in Los Angeles. At the center of the auction is a story two decades in the making: Marshall Mathers’ enduring commitment to philanthropy through footwear. What began in 2006 with a Nike Air Max charity series in the wake of his close friend Proof’s death has grown into one of the most consistent charitable threads in modern music culture, with every step tied to a larger purpose. title: One Goal: An Auction To Benefit The Fifa Global Citizen Education Fund Totals: $652,630
summary: When the clock finally ran out of time after a week of bidding, One Goal: An Auction To Benefit The Fifa Global Citizen Education Fund produced a statement win: All 27 lots sold for $652,630, a sum more than eight times the initial low estimate of what the sale would make. Fans from 24 nations in every region of the globe participated in intense online bidding that produced some big results. The two top lots of the sale both made $110,000. One of these was a ball used in the World Cup Final game at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford N.J, which saw Spain take the title against Argentina 1-0. The other top lot was part of a story followed avidly by social media and the press while bidding was ongoing: The competition for articles of clothing worn by the K-Pop phenomenon, BTS, during their iconic performance at the first-ever FIFA World Cup 2026™ Final Topps Halftime Show. title: 17th-century Dutch winter landscapes offer cool refuge from summer heat
summary: When it's 90 degrees outside and the sidewalks seem to radiate heat, there's something especially refreshing about looking at a Dutch winter landscape. You can almost feel the crisp air, hear the crunch of ice under your feet, and essentially forget that it's the middle of summer. That is exactly what these two 17th century paintings offer. They both take us into the heart of a Dutch winter, but they tell two very different stories. One gives us a quiet, reflective moment, and the other throws us into the middle of a busy day on the ice. Jan van de Cappelle's A Winter Landscape with Figures is all about atmosphere. There isn't much action. title: Princeton University Library exhibition showcasing artistry of rare Japanese illustrated books
summary: Princeton University Library celebrates the art and evolution of Japanese publishing with a new exhibition “The Art of Japanese Publishing: A Selection of Japanese Illustrated Books from the Marquand Library Collection 1660-1960,” curated by Nicole Fabricand-Person, Japanese Art Specialist, Marquand Library of Art & Archaeology and Holly Hatheway, Director, Marquand Library of Art & Archaeology. Featuring selections from Marquand Library’s collection of rare Japanese illustrated books from the 17th century through the 20th century, the exhibition opens Wednesday, September 9 in the Ellen and Leonard Milberg Gallery at Firestone Library, and will be on display through Sunday, December 6. The advent of commercial publishing in 17th-century Japan completely revolutionized the Japanese art tradition. title: Frye Art Museum announces acquisitions from Assembly Art Fair
summary: The Frye Art Museum announces three acquisitions made through its new partnership with Assembly Art Fair, welcoming the first works by Carly Feddersen (b. 1982, Wenatchee, WA, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation), Joe Feddersen (b. 1953, Omak, WA, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation), and Marie Watt (b.1967, Seattle, WA, Seneca Nation of Indians) into the museum’s collection. Made possible with support from the museum’s Lele Barnett Acquisition Fund, the purchases reflect the Frye's commitment to supporting artists whose practices are rooted in the Pacific Northwest while contributing to broader conversations in contemporary art. title: First Margaret Preston retrospective in more than 20 years opening at NGV this September
summary: Celebrated for her bold floral still lifes and strikingly modern woodblock prints, iconic Australian artist Margaret Preston (1875–1963) was a central figure in the development of modernism in Australia who significantly shaped the country’s cultural and aesthetic landscape. The first exhibition on the artist in more than two decades, Margaret Preston, charts the artist’s entire career through more than 200 of her paintings, prints and sculpture, alongside archival materials. The landmark exhibition also contextualises Preston’s practice and legacy by placing her work in direct dialogue with that of her peers, as well as work by contemporary First Nation artists. title: Rago/Wright appoints Lilly Dawson as Associate Director, Fine Art in Los Angeles
summary: Rago/Wright announced that Lilly Dawson has joined as Associate Director, Fine Art based in the firm's Los Angeles office. This appointment strengthens the firm's West Coast presence with a seasoned specialist whose career spans more than three decades at leading auction houses, galleries and private advisory, and whose expertise encompasses American, Impressionist, Modern and Contemporary art. Dawson joins Rago/Wright from her own practice, Gray Dawson Art Advisory which she has run since 2023 advising clients across London, Los Angeles and New York on Impressionist, Modern and Contemporary art. title: Aguttes highlights record-setting sales and standout lots from first half of 2026
summary: From a million-euro Vietnamese painting and a rare Ferrari to a Michael Jackson stage glove and a 21-carat Colombian emerald, Aguttes has taken stock of some of the strongest results achieved across its departments during the first half of 2026. The Paris auction house’s six-month review reflects the breadth of its specialties, ranging from fine jewelry, watches and classic cars to Asian art, Old Masters, modern and contemporary art, design, sports memorabilia and pop culture. Among the most significant results of the season was a work by Vietnamese painter Nguyễn Văn Thọ, known as Nam Sơn, which crossed the €1 million mark and established a new world auction record for the artist. The Luxury & Art de vivre departments produced several notable results during the opening months of the year. summary: Julien’s Auctions announced today “Atomic Kitsch: The Allee Willis Collection,” the industry leading entertainment auction house’s exclusive auction event celebrating the extraordinary life and career of the renowned visual artist, art director, sculptor, art collector and Grammy-Award winning, Tony- and Emmy-nominated songwriter who brought the world some of the biggest hit songs of all time including Earth, Wind & Fire’s “September” and “Boogie Wonderland,” and the Friends theme song “I'll Be There For You,” taking place Tuesday, August 18th, 2026 10am PT online at juliensauctions.com. title: Tanya Crane explores identity and African history in new Racine Art Museum jewelry show
summary: Responding to her own biracial background, Tanya Crane imbues her enamel, metal, and found object jewelry with reflections on history, resiliency, migration, community, adornment, humanity, identity, family, and heritage. As she considers how traditions shift across space or through time, Crane creates patterns that echo designs of global Indigenous makers. This exhibition features jewelry inspired by historical adornment in RAM’s permanent collection—specifically, incised metal bracelets and neckpieces from West Africa that were used as currency. Objects like this were exchanged within trade or barter networks, not only for local agricultural and luxury products but also in transatlantic slave trade negotiations. This potential compelled Crane to cautiously move forward with her explorations. title: Crystal Bridges unveils new 'Art Everywhere' program
summary: As part of Crystal Bridges’ 114,000 square foot expansion, the museum has launched a new public art initiative aimed at expanding the role of contemporary art on its campus. Art Everywhere transforms unexpected areas into immersive art experiences, blurring the boundaries between collection galleries and the transitional spaces that connect them. Through site-responsive commissions by ten artists, Art Everywhere activates high-traffic and unconventional locations throughout Crystal Bridges and the Momentary, including hallways, stairwells, elevators, crosswalks, and even restrooms, and invites visitors to encounter art in new, memorable ways. title: The Carle announces new Chief Curator and Director of Education
summary: The Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art announced two new senior staff who will help lead the Museum: Rebecca Klassen as Chief Curator, and Craig Langlois as Director of Education. “We are thrilled to welcome Rebecca to The Carle and are delighted that Craig is already making such a positive impact as a member of our leadership team,” said Jennifer Schantz, Executive Director of The Carle. “As we advance our strategic plan, Rebecca’s deep curatorial experience and commitment to research and scholarship will help to continue establishing The Carle as the leading voice in picture book art, while Craig’s innovative approach to education and community engagement is expanding opportunities for visitors of all ages to connect with the art, artists, and stories that inspire us. title: Joseph Bellows Gallery presents John Banasiak's 'George Brown's Bar' photographs online
summary: Joseph Bellows Gallery is presenting George Brown's Bar, an online exhibition of photographs by John Banasiak documenting the life of a neighborhood tavern on Chicago's South Side during the early 1970s. Created while Banasiak worked weekends tending bar, these photographs offer an intimate portrait of a close-knit working-class community at a moment when the neighborhood bar still served as the social and cultural heart of everyday American life. Rather than approaching his subjects as an outside observer, Banasiak photographed people he knew. Regular patrons, families, veterans, laborers, musicians, and friends appear throughout the series with a familiarity that could only have come through trust and shared experience. title: Singapore Art Museum presents Maria Taniguchi: Afterimage
summary: Singapore Art Museum is presenting Maria Taniguchi: Afterimage, the first monographic museum exhibition of the acclaimed artist in Singapore. Taking its title from visual sensations that linger in a viewer’s field of vision, Afterimage highlights recurring concerns that run through Taniguchi’s practice, including repetition, time, and labour. The exhibition is anchored by Taniguchi’s “brick paintings” (2008–ongoing), towering canvases made by individually filling hand-drawn rectangular cells. Rather than a deliberate response to the art historical legacy of modernism, the brick-like geometric pattern that repeats across Taniguchi’s canvases reflect the embodied process of their own production. title: Missoula Art Museum galleries partially close for major exhibition installation
summary: Throughout August, the Missoula Art Museum (MAM) will temporarily close three of its four galleries as staff prepares for the installation of Joe Feddersen: Earth, Water, Sky, opening during First Friday on September 4. While portions of the museum will be closed, MAM remains open and invites visitors to explore exhibitions from its collection, experience artworks in the MAM Art Park, and enjoy a new partnership that celebrates Missoula's vibrant arts community. On view is Land and the Cosmic: Works from the MAM Collection, an exhibition that explores the landscape as memory, identity, and kinship through works that examine our relationship to place. title: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi to open in December
summary: The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi has announced that Guggenheim Abu Dhabi will open its doors on December 11, 2026, further strengthening Abu Dhabi’s position as a leading global capital for the arts. Guggenheim Abu Dhabi is a museum of modern and contemporary art and will be a space for encounter and exchange, promoting a more connected and diverse global community through art. The museum has a unique identity and vision, shaped by Abu Dhabi’s artistic landscape and designed to reflect the United Arab Emirates’ stories and beyond, encouraging curiosity among younger generations about modern and contemporary art. title: Neon Museum to host Steve Wynn talk on history of The Mirage
summary: The Neon Museum – the Las Vegas non-profit illuminating the city’s cultural legacy through historic signage and storytelling – will present "Reflections of The Mirage: A Conversation with Steve Wynn” on October 22. Taking place in the showroom at Golden Nugget Las Vegas, the evening will examine the conception, development and legacy of The Mirage Resort & Casino, a project that helped usher in a new era for Las Vegas and the modern destination resort. “The Mirage represents a pivotal chapter of modern Las Vegas. The conversation will focus on 1987 - 1992 and provide an opportunity for Mr. Wynn to reflect on the concept, construction, opening, and operations of a resort whose influence continues to be felt today," said Aaron Berger, CEO of The Neon Museum. title: Tang Teaching Museum announces year-long interdisciplinary exhibition 'A Feeling of With'
summary: The Frances Young Tang Teaching Museum and Art Gallery presents A Feeling of With, a year-long exhibition featuring three interconnected explorations of how people understand themselves in relation to one another and the world. On view August 8, 2026, through July 18, 2027, A Feeling of With is organized by Rachel Seligman, Assistant Director for Curatorial Affairs and Malloy Curator, in collaboration with six Skidmore College faculty members from English, dance, art history, environmental studies and sciences, mathematics, and religious studies. Across three galleries, relation becomes both the exhibition’s subject and the structure through which artworks, disciplines, and ways of knowing encounter one another. title: First New York solo museum exhibition of Diego Marcon to feature new commission
summary: The New Museum presents the first New York museum solo exhibition of artist Diego Marcon (b. 1985, Busto Arsizio, Italy; lives and works in Lombardy, Italy), whose work in moving image and installation coopts familiar forms from horror movies, slapstick comedy, and cartoons to subvert cinematic archetypes and call into question accepted norms of family life and childhood. On view September 24, 2026, through January 31, 2027, Arrivederci, Piggies! stages four of Marcon’s most significant films as a total installation, including his newly commissioned film Krapfen. This film merges human choreography with green-screen CGI to explore the relationship between a child and their family, who are represented by floating articles of clothing.
